title: Identification of a novel gene signature predicting response to first-line chemotherapy in BRCA wild-type high-grade serous ovarian cancer patients.
authors: Buttarelli, Marianna; Ciucci, Alessandra; Palluzzi, Fernando; Raspaglio, Giuseppina; Marchetti, Claudia; Perrone, Emanuele; Minucci, Angelo; Giaco, Luciano; Fagotti, Anna; Scambia, Giovanni; Gallo, Daniela
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过RNA-seq和机器学习识别卵巢癌化疗反应基因签名，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) has poor survival rates due to a combination of diagnosis at advanced stage and disease recurrence as a result of chemotherapy resistance. In BRCA1 (Breast Cancer gene 1) - or BRCA2-wild type (BRCAwt) HGSOC patients, resistance and progressive disease occur earlier and more often than in mutated BRCA. Identification of biomarkers helpful in predicting response to first-line chemotherapy is a challenge to improve BRCAwt HGSOC management. METHODS: To identify a gene signature that can predict response to first-line chemotherapy, pre-treatment tumor biopsies from a restricted cohort of BRCAwt HGSOC patients were profiled by RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) technology. Patients were sub-grouped according to platinum-free interval (PFI), into sensitive (PFI > 12 months) and resistant (PFI < 6 months). The gene panel identified by RNA-seq analysis was then tested by high-throughput quantitative real-time PCR (HT RT-qPCR) in a validation cohort, and statistical/bioinformatic methods were used to identify eligible markers and to explore the relevant pathway/gene network enrichments of the identified gene set. Finally, a panel of primary HGSOC cell lines was exploited to uncover cell-autonomous mechanisms of resistance. RESULTS: RNA-seq identified a 42-gene panel discriminating sensitive and resistant BRCAwt HGSOC patients and pathway analysis pointed to the immune system as a possible driver of chemotherapy response. From the extended cohort analysis of the 42 DEGs (differentially expressed genes), a statistical approach combined with the random forest classifier model generated a ten-gene signature predictive of response to first-line chemotherapy. The ten-gene signature included: CKB (Creatine kinase B), CTNNBL1 (Catenin, beta like 1), GNG11 (G protein subunit gamma 11), IGFBP7 (Insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 7), PLCG2 (Phospholipase C, gamma 2), RNF24 (Ring finger protein 24), SLC15A3 (Solute carrier family 15 member 3), TSPAN31 (Tetraspanin 31), TTI1 (TELO2 interacting protein 1) and UQCC1 (Ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase complex assembly factor). Cytotoxicity assays, combined with gene-expression analysis in primary HGSOC cell lines, allowed to define CTNNBL1, RNF24, and TTI1 as cell-autonomous contributors to tumor resistance. CONCLUSIONS: Using machine-learning techniques we have identified a gene signature that could predict response to first-line chemotherapy in BRCAwt HGSOC patients, providing a useful tool towards personalized treatment modalities.
abstract_zh:
背景：高级别浆液性卵巢癌（HGSOC）因晚期诊断和化疗耐药导致的疾病复发，生存率较低。在BRCA1（乳腺癌基因1）或BRCA2野生型（BRCAwt）HGSOC患者中，耐药和疾病进展发生得更早且更频繁，相较于BRCA突变患者。识别有助于预测一线化疗反应的生物标志物，是改善BRCAwt HGSOC管理的一个挑战。

方法：为识别可预测一线化疗反应的基因特征，对一组受限的BRCAwt HGSOC患者治疗前肿瘤活检样本进行了RNA测序（RNA-Seq）分析。根据无铂间期（PFI），将患者分为敏感组（PFI > 12个月）和耐药组（PFI < 6个月）。通过RNA-seq分析识别的基因面板，随后在验证队列中采用高通量实时定量PCR（HT RT-qPCR）进行测试，并利用统计/生物信息学方法识别合格标记物，并探索所识别基因集的相关通路/基因网络富集。最后，利用一组原代HGSOC细胞系揭示细胞自主耐药机制。

结果：RNA-seq识别出一个42基因面板，可区分敏感和耐药的BRCAwt HGSOC患者，通路分析指出免疫系统可能是化疗反应的驱动因素。在扩展队列分析中，对42个差异表达基因（DEGs）采用统计方法结合随机森林分类器模型，生成了一个十基因特征，可预测一线化疗反应。该十基因特征包括：CKB（肌酸激酶B）、CTNNBL1（连环蛋白，β样1）、GNG11（G蛋白亚基γ11）、IGFBP7（胰岛素样生长因子结合蛋白7）、PLCG2（磷脂酶C，γ2）、RNF24（环指蛋白24）、SLC15A3（溶质载体家族15成员3）、TSPAN31（四跨膜蛋白31）、TTI1（TELO2相互作用蛋白1）和UQCC1（泛醇-细胞色素c还原酶复合物组装因子）。细胞毒性实验结合原代HGSOC细胞系中的基因表达分析，确定了CTNNBL1、RNF24和TTI1为肿瘤耐药的细胞自主贡献因子。

结论：利用机器学习技术，我们识别了一个基因特征，可预测BRCAwt HGSOC患者对一线化疗的反应，为个性化治疗模式提供了有用工具。
